Definition: Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country
BiblicalUsage: Anamim is named twice, in the same list both times: Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim. He was a son of Mizraim — Egypt — and the name stands for both the man and his descendants, a people of Egypt whose land and story the Bible never tells beyond the list.
TheologicalSignificance: A name in a list is all we have of Anamim, and I believe the list is enough: the sons of Mizraim are counted, and Egypt's peoples are named, because the table of nations is God's record of the whole earth.
